sections.overview: This geometrid moth is widespread across much of Europe and temperate Asia, reaching Japan.
sections.identification: The adult has a wingspan of about 33–36 mm.
sections.habitat: It uses open woodland, scrubby slopes and riverine woodland, often where privet grows.
sections.diet: The larvae feed on woody plants, especially privet and ash.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in early spring, mainly March and April in Britain.
sections.reproduction: Larvae feed in late spring, and the pupa overwinters.
sections.ecology: T. carpinata is a related spring moth recorded on willows and poplars; see its profile for comparison.
sections.conservation: The British account describes scattered local populations; this regional pattern is not a global conservation assessment.
